summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Pleats Mini Class ## Introduction The main function of the creation of pants as cloth is to solidify the structure. Before we can utilize the solidification process, we need to prepare the file to a state that can facilitate this. ## Preparing for Solidification Since the cutting operation will cause the solidification area to be deleted, it is essential to ensure that the individual shape solidification areas are free from cutting operations. ### Improving Cloth Quality To enhance the quality of the clothing, we need to reduce the particle strength, which in turn improves the texture of the cloth. Additionally, reducing the conflict thickness minimizes the air thickness between the plates, allowing them to stick tighter together. ### Fabric Selection When selecting suitable fabric for pants, it is recommended to use cotton down-line high bedding fabric. This fabric is advantageous as it does not easily stretch and results in a slightly firmer finish. ## Adjusting the Design After changing the fabric, you may notice some flaws. To prevent excessive solidification effects, modify all areas that require changes, such as the length of the pants. ### Length Adjustment When adjusting the length of garments that have numerous sewing lines and internal lines, pulling the bottom directly may cause deviations in the sewing lines. To mitigate this effect, utilize the pictured screen expansion feature. This property is typically not engaged when altering sewing line flow. ### Modifying Solidification Areas It is crucial to make all necessary modifications to prevent excessive solidification. The sewing line should remain consistent; however, be aware that the sleeve line cannot change in parallel with adjacent elements. ## Movement Adjustments Once all preparations are complete, you can begin altering the movement of the garment. The folds of the fabric often result from the movement of the human body. ### Editing Movements To modify movements in the software, press Shift + X to access the Google display. After opening the symmetrical edit, you can adjust the movements while the simulation is running. - Slowly drag the axis on the positional ball to rotate the thigh and induce contractions in the body. - As you adjust the movement, you will observe the gradual formation of the fabric folds. ## Enhancing Natural Movement To create more natural movements, you can manually drag the coat of arms. For tighter movements, use the Left and Right arrow keys for adjustments. Changes can also be made to the arm's motion. ### Part-Dimensional Solidification Once the effects appear satisfactory, utilize the selection grid brush tool to select specific grid sections for part-dimensional solidification. I prefer to select a smaller area of wrinkles for a more natural appearance. ## Wrinkle Management After part-dimensional solidification, the model's movement will adjust to a standard A pose. You can also implement Morph Targets. As the movement alters, the wrinkles will not revert to their original form. New wrinkles will appear in corresponding areas, such as the butt, mimicking special movement effects. If the transition remains unnatural, consider deleting the original solidification area and re-creating a part-dimensional solidification. With these adjustments, the wrinkles can be retained indefinitely. ## Conclusion After completing the transitions, continue to refine your design process. Use the tree feature to draw individual elements effectively. ### Final Touches After making adjustments, ensure that the Random Light feature does not display any red or yellow markings. I hope you enjoyed this tutorial. In the next video, I will demonstrate how to erase unwanted elements. See you next time! ```
